messages.subject: weight vector and stack
parts:
How should I pass vector of weights (say w) to an f-term to inla when using a stack?

I.e. I have something like :
formula=y~-1+one+x+f(D,w,model="iid")
(just for illustration, later on, I would like to have it more complicated and with other than iid terms e.g. for varying-coefficient submodels)

and do not know where to put w in the inla call.

First, there seems to be no place for additional argument in inla.stack call. 

So, I tried to pass w to inla via setting it as a global variable before calling inla, like 
w<-something
inla(...)

or by enlarging the data list as 
l<-inla.stack.data(stack)
l[["w"]<-as.vector(something)
and then using inla(..., data=l)

or by using
data=inla.stack.data(stack,list(w=something))
which I thought is what the ?inla.stack help says for the case 
inla.stack.data(stack,...)

but with no success in either case.

How to do it correctly?

All the Best
 Marek

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] weight vector and stack
parts:
﻿
﻿Hi,
When using the stack construction of a model, one approach is to apply the weights to the A-matrix that is applied to that model component instead of the f() function.
In your example case, I believe Diagonal(n, w) would give you the needed matrix.

inla.stack(data=…, A=list(Diagonal(n,w), 1), effects=list(list(D=D), list(x, one)))

For more complex models, e.g. spde models, just multiply the non-weighted matrix by that diagonal weight matrix (from the left or right, depending on the model definition…)

Finn
